candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care → Advocacy, printed p.20 / PDF p.24
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Advocacy / chain of command
candidate.educational_objective: Use the chain of command as an advocacy resource when a significant client-safety concern remains unresolved after appropriate initial reporting.

options.A: Use the organization's chain of command to continue advocating for the client
options.B: Stop pursuing the concern because it has already been mentioned once
options.C: Discuss the concern only with coworkers who are not responsible for resolving it
options.D: Delay further action until the next routine staff meeting

candidate.rationale: The 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan places advocacy within Management of Care and specifically includes using advocacy resources appropriately, including the chain of command. When a serious client-safety concern remains unresolved after an appropriate initial report, continuing through the chain of command is the best advocacy action. Stopping, discussing the issue only with uninvolved coworkers, or delaying escalation does not address the unresolved client-safety concern.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Entry-level RNs act as client advocates and appropriately use advocacy resources such as the chain of command.
candidate.source_locator: Detailed Test Plan, Management of Care → Advocacy, printed p.20 / PDF p.24: act in the role of client advocate; use advocacy resources appropriately (e.g., social worker, chain of command, interpreter)
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A nurse identifies a serious client-safety concern and reports it to the appropriate immediate team member, but the concern remains unresolved. What is the most appropriate next action?
